radioSource: ESP32-C3-MINI-1 & MINI-1U datasheet v2.2 (2026-05-06): Bluetooth LE transmit 170 mA peak at 0 dBm and receive 86 mA (Table 6-5); Wi-Fi transmit up to 350 mA (802.11b at 20.5 dBm, Table 6-4); external supply at least 0.5 A (Table 6-2), 3.3 V, 25 °C
notes: 4 MB on-module flash; it holds the firmware and the reading history (NVS or a LittleFS partition), so no external memory part is needed (datasheet v2.2, ESP32-C3-MINI-1-N4). Its USB Serial/JTAG controller on GPIO18 (USB_D-) and GPIO19 (USB_D+) programs the flash over USB, so flashing over USB-C needs no USB-UART bridge (datasheet v2.2, section 5.2.1.5 and the pin table). It runs from a 3.0–3.6 V supply (datasheet v2.2, recommended operating conditions). Its chip's current (ESP32-C3 Series Datasheet v2.4, 3.3 V, 25 °C): CPU running at 160 MHz with the radio off 23–28 mA (Table 5-8); radio receiving 84 mA and Wi-Fi transmitting up to 335 mA peak (Table 5-7, 100% duty); deep sleep 5 µA (Table 5-9). The chip datasheet gives no Bluetooth LE current figure; the module datasheet v2.2 does (bleTxMa, bleRxMa). Its strapping pins are GPIO2, GPIO8 and GPIO9 (datasheet v2.4, section 3.1): GPIO9 low when reset is released selects download boot (USB-Serial-JTAG or UART); GPIO0, GPIO1 and GPIO3 to GPIO5 are not strapping pins. Download boot also needs GPIO8 high at reset (Technical Reference Manual v1.4, Table 7.2-1: GPIO9 0 with GPIO8 0 is SPI download boot or, with GPIO2 0, an invalid combination); GPIO8 floats by default (datasheet v2.4, Table 3-1) and the module has no pull-up on it (module datasheet v2.2, Figure 8-1), so the board fits one (Espressif's peripheral schematic, Figure 9-1, R8 10k). GPIO2 only counts when GPIO8 and GPIO9 are both low; the datasheet still recommends a pull-up on it "due to glitches" without saying which

radioSource: ESP32-S3-MINI-1 & MINI-1U datasheet v1.7: Bluetooth LE transmit 189 mA at 0 dBm and receive 93 mA (Table 6-5); Wi-Fi 802.11b transmit up to 355 mA peak (Table 6-4); external supply at least 0.5 A, 3.3 V
notes: The robot MCU when the ESP32-C3's pins run out: 39 GPIOs (the C3-MINI-1 has 15) and four hardware pulse counters (PCNT) that decode both encoder channels in quadrature (ESP32-S3 Technical Reference Manual, Pulse Count Controller). ESP32-S3-MINI-1-N8: 8 MB flash, no PSRAM, so GPIO26 is free (datasheet v1.7, Table 3-1 note b). Its USB Serial/JTAG controller on GPIO19 (USB_D-) and GPIO20 (USB_D+) programs it over USB-C with no bridge; UART0 on GPIO43/GPIO44 (TXD0/RXD0). Strapping pins GPIO0, GPIO3, GPIO45, GPIO46: GPIO0 low at reset enters download boot (GPIO46 must then be low, its default pull-down); keep GPIO3/45/46 free of loads that pull them at reset. Currents (datasheet v1.7, 3.3 V, 25 °C): dual core at 240 MHz 66.2 mA (Table 6-6), deep sleep 8 µA (Table 6-7). Firmware simulation: none here (Xtensa; the drive simulation runs on the ESP32-C3 in QEMU riscv32), so an S3 robot's report says drive sim not run. LCSC C2913206, a JLCPCB extended part, $4.68 each or $3.32 at 100 (jlcsearch, 17 Nov 2026).

notes: Single-cell Li-ion linear charger, 4.2 V float (4.158 to 4.242 V; the -42 suffix is this voltage, not a current). Charge current is set by the PROG resistor to ground, about 1000 V / RPROG: 10 kOhm 100 mA, 5 kOhm 200 mA, 2 kOhm 500 mA (465 to 535 mA), 1.4 kOhm 600 mA, 500 mA max by programming; the board generator fits 4.7 kOhm, about 210 mA (0.4 C on a 500 mAh cell). Pins (SOT-23-5): 1 CHRG open drain, low while charging, high impedance when done; 2 GND; 3 BAT; 4 VCC 4.25 to 6.5 V with at least 1 uF; 5 PROG. Ends the charge at 1/10 of the set current. notes: JST PH 2-pin, top entry: a motor's two wires (2 A per contact, JST PH catalogue).

JST SH 6-pin, 1 mm pitch, side entry (https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C160405.html): an encoder gearmotor's plug, in Pololu's pin order (https://www.pololu.com/product/5139: 1 GND, 2 encoder B, 3 encoder A, 4 encoder Vcc 2.7-18 V, 5 M2, 6 M1). The board generator wires M1/M2 to the motor driver's outputs and VCC to 3V3; the architect puts ENCA on a GPIO (ENC_LA on the left motor's plug JM1, ENC_RA on the right's JM2; ENCB stays unconnected: the firmware counts channel A's edges, its direction from the duty). The encoder pulls its outputs up itself (10 kOhm). JST SH contacts carry 1 A (JST SH catalogue): enough for a 0.67 A stall.

JST XH 2-pin, 2.5 mm pitch, top entry: the emergency stop button's two wires (its NC contact). The board generator puts it in the motor supply: VBAT on pin 1, the driver's VM (net MOTOR_VM) on pin 2, so pressing the button opens the motors' supply. XH, not PH, so it can't be swapped with a motor plug. 3 A per contact (JST XH catalogue); LCSC https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C158012.html.

2-pin 2.54 mm straight male header (XFCN, https://www.lcsc.com/product-detail/C492401.html): a pull-cord start. The cord ends in a 2-way 2.54 mm socket with a wire loop that shorts START to GND while it is in; pulling the cord pulls it off (no latch, so it comes away: Eurobot General Rules 1.2 F.6). The board generator pulls START up (10 kOhm to 3V3); the architect puts START on a GPIO (pins: signal START, partPin START).
